actions: ran matched-budget two-evaluator synthetic archive experiments with controlled cross-evaluator dependence
swept evaluator-B symmetric error from 0.40 to 0.20 and cross dependence from 0 to 1 under fixed 1200-call budget
persisted exact reproducibility script and clean checkpoint
headline_result: With equal marginal evaluator error q=0.40, switching from a correlated evaluator to B improved archive quality only when cross-evaluator error dependence was low; the paired gain fell from +0.0230 +/- 0.0126 at cross=0 to +0.0005 +/- 0.0141 at cross=1. A materially stronger B remained valuable despite high correlation. In the asymmetric q_FA(A)=0.40/q_FR(A)=0.20 regime, reducing B false-admission error alone did not produce a reliable quality gain under the tested symmetric LR gate.
scope: Role-local synthetic evidence only; no external LLM performance threshold is claimed. Public judge-panel sources support the separate premise that nominal multi-model diversity can have low effective independence.
termination_cause: semantic freeze barrier: newer note main observed after semantic work; checkpointed completed work under frozen tuple and stopped new semantic work
exact_next_action: Resolve and freeze the then-current control tuple, then compare same-evaluator replay, naive A×B LR, dependence-discounted B evidence, and separate-B confirmation with abstention under symmetric and asymmetric error regimes; measure archive quality, false authoritative promotions, throughput, raw verifier calls, and effective evidence per call.
